S7.01.note: The centred start view is built in apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx (testID chat.new-chat.middle). ChatEmptyState.tsx is not referenced from any file under apps/mobile/app. The greeting wording changes with the time of day.
steps: Sign in with a signed-in account.
Look at the first screen before typing: it should open on the new chat, not a chat that already has messages.
If a conversation is open, tap "Open menu" (top left), then tap "New chat" in the sidebar.
Compare: the greeting and the message box sit in the middle of the empty area, not at the top of an empty transcript.
S7.01.where: First screen after sign-in (the new chat). On a phone, tap "Open menu" then "New chat" from a conversation.

S7.02.note: No reading-width cap found for chat messages. MessageBubble.tsx uses maxWidth '85%' (lines 686, 2301), and MessageList.tsx does not use contentColumn. contentColumn('reading') in apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts is used only by other screens (Toast, ApprovalModal, AgentsScreen, CustomizeScreen and similar) and MemoryUsedChip/ConversationExportSheet. Searched apps/mobile for contentColumn( and READING_COLUMN_MAX_WIDTH.

S7.12.note: On a wide window the sidebar stays permanently open and the "Open menu" button is not shown (the slot is blank).
steps: Sign in and open any chat from the list.
Tap "Open menu" at the top left of the chat header.
Look: the sidebar slides over the chat.
Tap the dimmed area beside the sidebar, or swipe it left, to close it.
Tap "Open menu" again and compare: the sidebar reopens.
S7.12.where: Conversation screen on a phone-width window: tap "Open menu" at the top left to open the sidebar, and close it again.

S7.15.note: The "Expand message" button only appears once the text is multi-line. The close control's visible words were not found in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx, so check its label on screen.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Type several lines into the message box until it grows.
Tap the "Expand message" button at the top right of the box.
Look: a full-screen editor covers the screen with the same text and a send control.
Close the editor and check you are back in the chat with your text kept.
S7.15.where: Chat message box: tap "Expand message" at its top right corner after typing a long message.

S7.16.needs: a saved research report on the account
S7.16.note: "Reports" appears in the sidebar only when the research feature is switched on. The empty state says "Research reports are saved to your Managed Cloud account."
steps: Tap "Open menu" (top left) in a chat to open the sidebar.
Tap "Reports".
Tap a report in the list.
Look: the report opens on a full screen with a "Reports" header and a back control, and the report text fills the screen.
S7.16.where: Sidebar > Reports > tap a report in the list.

S7.17.needs: a chat with an image in it
S7.17.note: The viewer's close and counter wording was not confirmed by exact visible text. The "Open image" link in MarkdownImage.tsx opens an outside browser, not this viewer.
steps: Open a chat that has an image in it (a photo you sent, or a generated image).
Tap the image.
Look: the image opens over the chat on a full-screen dark viewer.
Use the viewer's close control, or swipe it away, and check you are back in the chat.
S7.17.where: A chat that contains an image: tap the image in the message.

S7.20.needs: a chat with enough messages to scroll
steps: Open a chat with many messages.
Scroll the transcript up and down.
Look: the message box stays fixed at the bottom while the messages move above it.
S7.20.where: Any long chat: the message box at the bottom of the screen.

S7.21.note: The code caps the box at a maximum height of 160 and scrolls past that; compare what you see with that.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Type a long prompt of several sentences into the message box.
Look: the box grows taller as you type instead of staying one line.
Once it is multi-line, check the "Expand message" button appears at the top right of the box.
S7.21.where: Chat message box: type a long prompt; the box grows and shows "Expand message" at its top right.

S7.22.needs: a chat with a long transcript
steps: Open a chat with a long history.
Scroll the messages up and down.
Look: the header at the top and the message box at the bottom do not move while the messages scroll.
S7.22.where: Any chat with a long transcript: the messages scroll, the header and message box stay in place.

S7.23.needs: a chat that has an artifact in it
S7.23.note: "Copy content" is a default value passed to copyControlLabel in the file, so the on-screen text may change with copy status.
steps: Open a chat where the assistant made an artifact (a document or code).
Tap the artifact card in the reply.
Look at the top toolbar: "Download artifact", "Copy content" and "More artifact actions" should be visible.
Scroll the artifact body down.
Compare: the toolbar stays at the top while the content scrolls.
S7.23.where: An artifact card in a chat reply: tap the card, then look at the toolbar at the top of the full-screen artifact.

S7.25.needs: a window that can be resized (tablet or wide simulator)
S7.25.note: The threshold is in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts (280 sidebar plus 720 content). The app's _layout.tsx uses useTabletLayout, which was not opened.
steps: Open a chat in a narrow window (phone size).
Tap "Open menu": the sidebar slides over the chat.
Widen the window (iPad or wide simulator) past about 1000 points.
Look: the sidebar now stays beside the chat and "Open menu" is gone.
S7.25.where: Chat screen when the window is resized: narrow windows show the sidebar over the chat, wide windows keep it beside the chat.

S7.26.note: The model picker is also a bottom sheet, but the only entry found in code is "Choose a model", shown when the retired-model notice appears (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx). The regular model entry was not confirmed.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat".
Tap "Add to chat" beside the message box.
Look: a sheet rises from the bottom of the screen with attachment, mode and feature options.
Drag the sheet down, or tap outside it, to close.
Compare: the options appear as a bottom sheet, not a small popover.
S7.26.where: Chat message box: tap "Add to chat" to open a bottom sheet.

S7.27.note: Threshold in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts. The sidebar is a permanent drawer in apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx.
steps: Open the app on an iPad simulator, or widen the window past about 1000 points.
Open a chat.
Look: the sidebar stays on the left as a fixed column and the chat sits beside it.
Tap a different chat in the sidebar and check the chat on the right changes.
S7.27.where: Chat screen on a tablet-width window: the sidebar stays on the left and the chat fills the right.

steps: Open a chat on an iPhone simulator.
Look: the header sits below the notch and the message box above the home indicator.
Tap the message box so the keyboard opens.
Look: the message box rises above the keyboard and the latest message stays visible.
S7.28.where: Chat screen on a phone: header clear of the notch, message box clear of the home bar, and the layout lifts when the keyboard opens.

S7.29.needs: a window that can be resized
S7.29.note: Limits are constants in apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts. A minimum width for the chat column is not a separate control.
steps: Open a chat in a narrow window and tap "Open menu" to show the sidebar.
Look: the sidebar is at most 300 points wide and no more than 88 percent of the window.
Widen the window past about 1000 points and look: the sidebar is a fixed 280 points beside the chat.
S7.29.where: Sidebar width when the window is resized (wide or narrow).

S7.32.needs: a chat with messages (a printer is optional)
S7.32.note: Printing uses the system print dialog. Report printing was not found; only conversation printing was.
steps: Open a chat that has messages.
Tap "Conversation menu" at the top right.
Tap "Export".
Tap "Print" in the export sheet.
Look: the system print preview shows the conversation text without the app's buttons. Cancel the dialog.
S7.32.where: Conversation menu > Export > Print (top right of a chat).
